title: Strongly explicit Ramanujan families for every degree
formal: For every fixed integer \(d\ge 3\), is there one deterministic algorithm that computes the port rotation map of connected d-regular Ramanujan graphs for an unbounded set of vertex counts n in time polynomial in log n, with the effective family and graph conventions below?
definitions: The graphs are undirected multigraphs on \([n]=\{1,\ldots ,n\}\); parallel edges and loops are permitted, as in the source’s graph convention. Each vertex has ports \([d]\). A rotation map \(Rot_{n}:[n]\times [d]\to [n]\times [d]\) is an involution: if \(Rot_{n}(v,i)=(w,j)\), then \(Rot_{n}(w,j)=(v,i)\). Paired ports encode an undirected edge; a fixed port encodes a loop. Define the symmetric integer adjacency matrix A by \(A_{vw}=|\{i\in[d]:\operatorname{first}(\operatorname{Rot}_n(v,i))=w\}|\), so every row sum is d and a fixed-port loop contributes one to the diagonal and degree. Connectivity means the underlying undirected graph is connected. List the real eigenvalues with multiplicity in decreasing order \(d=\lambda _{1}\ge \cdots \ge \lambda _{n}\). Require \(|\lambda_i|\le2\sqrt{d-1}\) for \(i\ge 2\), except that the single eigenvalue −d is permitted when the graph is bipartite. For each fixed d the answer supplies a decidable infinite set \(N_{d}\) of positive integers, a single total deterministic bit algorithm \(R_{d}\), and constants \(C_{d},a_{d}\). On input \((n,v,i)\) in binary, \(R_{d}\) runs in at most \(C_d(1+\log_2 n)^{a_d}\) steps for valid \(v\in [n],i\in [d]\). For every \(n\in N_{d}\) its outputs constitute the rotation map of such a graph. No graph-dependent advice, preprocessing or tables are supplied to \(R_{d}\); its fixed program may depend on d. The family’s size-membership decider must halt on all binary n but has no prescribed running-time bound. No bound on gaps between successive \(n\in N_{d}\) is required. Outputs at n outside \(N_{d}\) carry no graph promise. This retains the imported infinite-family target, which is weaker than requiring every admissible size; it does not impose simple-graph or non-bipartite restrictions.

context_blocks.text: Ramanujan families attain the limiting optimal spectral bound for their fixed degree. Strong explicitness requires computing local connections in time polynomial in the vertex-label length.

The source distinguishes exact Ramanujan families for certain degrees from constructions with spectral slack for general degrees. This question retains an unbounded effective family for each fixed degree, without requiring every admissible graph size.

why: Combine extremal spectral quality with efficient local access for arbitrary constant-degree expanders.
answer_criterion: Provide a Lean proof of the quantified family construction, including a size-membership decider, the uniform local rotation algorithm, infinitely many sizes, connectivity and the exact spectral bound for every fixed degree. Alternatively provide a Lean refutation for some degree. Spectral slack, graph-specific advice or polynomial time in the vertex count does not satisfy strong explicitness.

sentences: A regular Ramanujan graph meets the optimal asymptotic bound on nontrivial adjacency eigenvalues.
The question asks for an infinite family at every fixed degree at least three.
One algorithm must compute each local port connection in time polynomial in the vertex-label length.
The family may use only a decidable unbounded set of sizes and permits the stated multigraph conventions.
Constructions with positive spectral slack or slower global access do not meet the exact strong-explicitness target.
